experiment: E17 UML3 palettes in CATIA Magic: custom symbolic view definitions whose palette buttons create UML3 keyword elements
setup: Slice E17a, loaded into the project that already holds the UML3 libraries and examples: customization/catia-magic/UML3CatiaMagic.sysml (template packages with one unnamed keyword element each, e.g. package classTemplate { #classType item def; }; UML3ClassPalette :> DS_Views::ViewPalettes::GeneralPalette with a 'UML3 Classifiers' and a 'UML3 Relationships' category of OperationFromTemplate buttons, plus predefined OperationFromCode buttons; view def 'UML3 Class Diagram' :> UML3Views::ClassDiagram, DS_Views::CoreViews::bsv and 'UML3 Class Detail Diagram' :> UML3Views::ClassDetailDiagram, bsv, each redefining baseViewPalette with UML3ClassPalette) and customization/catia-magic/examples/OnlineStoreCatiaMagicViews.sysml (views of OnlineStoreDomain typed by both). Checks: builder errors on load, validation engine on UML3CatiaMagic and OnlineStoreCatiaMagicViews, tools/cameo-scripts/verifyPalettes.groovy (DSLService visualization and palette: categories, buttons, operations, template elements and their keyword metadata), exportViewDiagrams.groovy (display mode, shapes, SVG labels, overlaps).

General View, Interconnection View); 'UML3 Class Diagram' is not among them and the views of both UML3 definitions get the General View visualization and palette (12 categories, no UML3 category). Cause found in the bytecode of com.dassault_systemes.modeler.sysml.dsl.a.g (read): the registry is built breadth-first from DS_Views::CoreViews::Visualization over subclassifications, keeping a subtype only when its FIRST owned subclassification targets the parent. 'UML3 Class Diagram' :> UML3Views::ClassDiagram, bsv has UML3Views::ClassDiagram first, so it is never reached; the vendor's own 'General View' :> bsv, gv lists bsv first. A view whose definition is not registered falls back by rendering kind to General View (symbolic) or Generic Table (tabular).

CATIA Magic accepts an owned rendering over inherited ones, although the SysML OCL counts inherited ViewRenderingMemberships too, so by the specification E17V2 and E17V3 still have more than one; E17V5 and E17V6 have one because their owned rendering redefines the inherited ones

conclusion: The customization works and is verified: 6 view definitions, 6 palettes and 41 templated buttons, each copying the expected element kind with its UML3 keyword; the UML3 Create View dialog is the active one; all 17 loaded packages validate with 0 failures; the six views render with the expected display mode and 0 overlapping shapes. Three rules for a custom view definition (vendor definition first; one owned rendering redefining the inherited ones; no detail views with palettes) are documented in docs/CATIA-MAGIC-CUSTOMIZATION.md. In the GUI the palette is built when the diagram is created: a diagram that existed before the customization was registered keeps the General View palette, and recreating it (or reloading the project) gives it the UML3 palette - see docs/images/uml3-catia-magic-palette.png, captured with tools/cameo-scripts/captureDiagramWindow.groovy.
furtherObservations: Validation engine, first full version: 4 validateConnectorRelatedFeatures errors, because a connector that is not abstract needs two related features; the assembly, delegation, deploy and manifest templates now own two placeholder ends and use the connect/allocate form

The ANTLR sysml-validator rejected three constructs that the specification allows: unnamed definitions (Identification is optional, 8.2.2.1), short names on package declarations, and a body on a render statement (ViewRenderingUsage ends with UsageBody, 8.2.2.26). All three were fixed in the validator with tests (sysmlv2-validator 1b53f03, 076ac16)

DSLService.resetCache() is enough to register a newly loaded customization in the running tool; the project does not have to be reloaded for the model-level palette, only for diagrams that already exist
